title: fido2: the first attestor that establishes presence
description:
hire-attestors/src/fido2.rs has a real is_available() backed by ctap_hid_fido2::get_fidokey_devices() (:34-40), but hire-attestors declares NO default features, so the fido2 feature is off and the whole module compiles out. And it inherits the default prove() regardless.

THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL CHILD IN THE EPIC, because it is the first source that can establish PRESENCE AT ALL. Today nothing can: the README records that the presence TTL is 'enforced -- but no attestor yet establishes presence at all, so the bound is checked against an observation that always reports no presence'. The entire persona-3tly presence model is theory tested against nothing. This is what tests it.

Mechanics: a CTAP2 assertion over the daemon's challenge. The UP bit proves a physical touch; the UV bit proves the authenticator verified the user (PIN or on-key biometric). SPEC-HIRE says iaa3 with hardware presence. Note persona-3tly.2 -- UP and UV are DIFFERENT FACTS and PresenceLevel currently collapses them. Do not paper over that here; this bead is the evidence that the collapse is real.

BLOCKED ON persona-jl4j.3 FOR A REASON. This is the first attestor that PROMPTS A HUMAN. The persona-jl4j decision is that FetchJWTSVID never prompts, enforced by a proof-cost field that does not exist yet. Landing fido2's prove() before that field exists puts a touch on every FetchJWTSVID for every consumer -- the exact consent-fatigue failure jl4j was filed to prevent.

Also decide whether the feature goes on by default. It is real code behind an off switch, so today it is dead weight in every build.
acceptance_criteria: A CTAP2 assertion over the daemon's challenge, UP and UV reported as distinct facts; the attestor declares itself prompting via persona-jl4j.3 and is excluded from the unprompted path; a decision recorded on default-feature status.
